stem: Which statement describes **asexual** reproduction?

options.content: One parent produces offspring that are genetically identical to it
options.rationale: No gametes are involved, so the offspring are clones.

options.content: Two gametes fuse to produce a zygote
options.rationale: That describes sexual reproduction.

options.content: Two parents produce offspring that are genetically different
options.rationale: That describes sexual reproduction.

options.content: Pollen is transferred from an anther to a stigma
options.rationale: That is pollination, part of sexual reproduction in flowering plants.

explanation: Asexual reproduction involves one parent and no gametes, so the offspring are genetically identical to the parent and to each other.
hints: A- means without: without sex cells.

stem: Which of these is an example of asexual reproduction?

options.content: New potato plants growing from the eyes of a potato tuber
options.rationale: A tuber produces genetically identical plants from its buds.

options.content: A maize grain forming after pollen lands on a silk
options.rationale: Grains form after fertilisation, which is sexual reproduction.

options.content: Bean seeds forming in a pod after fertilisation
options.rationale: Seeds are the result of sexual reproduction.

options.content: A pollen nucleus fusing with an egg cell
options.rationale: Fusion of gametes is sexual reproduction.

explanation: Growing new plants from a tuber involves no gametes; the new plants are clones of the parent. Seeds and grains are normally the product of sexual reproduction.
hints: Which option involves no gametes?

stem: Name the type of asexual reproduction in which a bacterial cell divides into two identical cells.

rejected.feedback: Budding is how yeast reproduces. Bacteria divide by binary fission.
Fusion means joining together. A bacterium splits into two, which is binary fission.

explanation: Bacteria reproduce asexually by binary fission: the cell copies its DNA and splits into two genetically identical cells.
hints: Binary means 'two'.

stem: A farmer in Burma Valley wants to plant more banana plants identical to her best ones. Which part should she plant?

options.content: Suckers from the base of the parent plants
options.rationale: Bananas are usually propagated from suckers, which are clones of the parent.

options.content: Seeds from the bananas she eats
options.rationale: Edible bananas are seedless, and seeds would not give identical plants.

options.content: Bulbs dug up from beside the plants
options.rationale: Bananas do not form bulbs; onions do.

options.content: Runners growing along the ground
options.rationale: Runners are found in plants such as strawberries, not bananas.

explanation: Banana plants produce suckers: new shoots that grow from buds on the underground stem. Planting suckers gives clones of the parent, which is how seedless edible bananas are propagated.
hints: Edible bananas have no seeds.

stem: True or false: offspring produced by asexual reproduction are genetically identical to their parent.

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Correct: with no fusion of gametes, the offspring are clones of the parent (unless a mutation occurs).
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: The statement is true. Asexual reproduction involves one parent and no gametes, so the offspring are clones.

explanation: In asexual reproduction all the offspring's genetic material comes from one parent, copied without any fusion of gametes, so the offspring are genetically identical to the parent.
hints: How many parents contribute genetic material?

stem: Which statement describes **sexual** reproduction?

options.content: The nuclei of two gametes fuse to form a zygote, giving genetically different offspring
options.rationale: Fusion of gametes is the defining feature of sexual reproduction.

options.content: A single cell splits into two identical cells
options.rationale: That is binary fission, a form of asexual reproduction.

options.content: A new plant grows from a piece of stem
options.rationale: That is a cutting, a form of asexual reproduction.

options.content: A bud grows out of a yeast cell and separates
options.rationale: That is budding, a form of asexual reproduction.

explanation: Sexual reproduction involves the fusion of the nuclei of a male and a female gamete (fertilisation) to form a zygote. The offspring are genetically different from each other and from their parents.
hints: Look for the option that involves gametes.

stem: A tomato leaf cell has 24 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in the nucleus of a tomato egg cell?

options.rationale: Gametes are haploid: they have one set of chromosomes, half the diploid number.
24 is the diploid number of body cells; gametes have half this.
48 is double the body-cell number; a gamete has half the diploid number, not twice it.
This is a quarter of the diploid number; gametes have exactly one set (half).

explanation: Body cells are diploid (two sets of chromosomes). Gametes are haploid (one set), so a tomato egg cell has 24 ÷ 2 = 12 chromosomes. Fertilisation restores 24 in the zygote. (Cambridge Supplement.)
hints: Gametes are haploid.

stem: Why do sugar cane growers prefer to plant stem pieces (setts) rather than seeds?

options.content: The new plants are identical to a high-yielding parent, so the crop is uniform
options.rationale: Asexual reproduction keeps the good features of the chosen variety.

options.content: Plants grown from setts show more variation, so they adapt better
options.rationale: Asexual reproduction produces no variation.

options.content: Plants grown from setts are always resistant to every disease
options.rationale: Clones share the same weaknesses; they are not resistant to every disease.

options.content: Setts contain more seeds than the flowers produce
options.rationale: Setts are stem pieces; they contain buds, not seeds.

explanation: Setts are stem cuttings, so every new plant is a clone of the chosen high-yielding variety. The crop grows evenly and matures at the same time, which suits large-scale harvesting.
hints: What do all clones have in common?

stem: A wild grass spreads across a valley entirely by underground rhizomes. What is the main danger of this for the population?

options.content: With no variation, a new disease or change in conditions could kill the whole population
options.rationale: All the plants are clones, so if one is susceptible, all are.

options.content: The plants will need pollinators to survive
options.rationale: Spreading by rhizomes needs no pollinators.

options.content: The plants will grow too slowly to colonise the valley
options.rationale: Vegetative spread is usually fast.

options.content: Each new plant will have half the parent's chromosomes
options.rationale: Asexual offspring have exactly the same chromosomes as the parent.

explanation: Rhizomes produce clones. Without genetic variation, the population cannot adapt by natural selection, so a new disease or a change in the environment could affect every plant in the same way.
hints: Think about variation.

stem: In grafting a mango tree, what is the **scion**?

options.content: The shoot of the variety with the desired fruit, joined onto another plant's roots
options.rationale: The scion grows into the fruiting part of the grafted tree.

options.content: The rooted plant onto which the shoot is joined
options.rationale: That is the rootstock.

options.content: The tape used to hold the cut surfaces together
options.rationale: The tape is just a binding, not part of the plant.

options.content: A seed planted next to the tree
options.rationale: Grafting is asexual propagation; no seed is involved.

explanation: In grafting, the scion (a shoot or bud of a variety with good fruit) is joined to a rootstock (a hardy rooted plant). The fruit produced is identical to that of the scion's parent.
hints: The other part is called the rootstock.

stem: Match each structure used in natural vegetative reproduction with a plant that uses it.
explanation: Potatoes form stem tubers, onions form bulbs, strawberries send out runners and ginger grows from rhizomes. Maize is grown from grains (seeds), the product of sexual reproduction.
hints: One plant in the list is grown from seed.

stem: A farmer cuts cassava stems into pieces to plant. Why must each piece include at least one node?

options.content: The buds that grow into new shoots are found at the nodes
options.rationale: Without a bud, a stem piece cannot produce a new shoot.

options.content: The nodes contain the seeds
options.rationale: Stems do not contain seeds.

options.content: The nodes are where pollination happens
options.rationale: Pollination happens in flowers, and cuttings involve no pollination.

options.content: The nodes store all the plant's water
options.rationale: Nodes are not water stores; their importance here is the buds.

explanation: Buds are found at the nodes of a stem. A cutting needs at least one bud to grow a new shoot, and roots form from the cut stem.
hints: What grows into a new shoot?

stem: Complete the sentences about chromosomes in human reproduction.

payload.template: A human sperm cell is {{blank:sperm}} and contains {{blank:number}} chromosomes. After fertilisation, the zygote is {{blank:zygote}}.

explanation: Gametes are haploid: a human sperm or egg has one set of 23 chromosomes. When they fuse, the zygote has two sets, 46 chromosomes, and is diploid. (Cambridge Supplement.)
hints: A human body cell has 46 chromosomes.

stem: In the twentieth century, a fungal disease destroyed the Gros Michel banana plantations of Central America, even though the plants were healthy and productive before the disease arrived. Which feature of the way they were grown made them so vulnerable?

options.content: They were all grown from suckers, so they were genetically identical and none had resistance
options.rationale: Clones share the same alleles; if one is susceptible, all are.

options.content: They were grown from seed, so they were too variable
options.rationale: Edible bananas are seedless and were grown from suckers.

options.content: Bananas cannot photosynthesise when infected by any fungus
options.rationale: This does not explain why every plantation was lost.

options.content: Bananas need insects to pollinate them
options.rationale: The plants were propagated from suckers, so pollination was irrelevant to the spread of disease.

explanation: Asexual propagation produced millions of identical plants. With no genetic variation, no plant carried resistance, so the disease could spread through every plantation.
hints: Think about variation in a crop grown from suckers.

stem: The leaf cells of a bean plant each contain 22 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are there in the nucleus of a bean egg cell?
explanation: Leaf cells are diploid (22 chromosomes, two sets of 11). An egg cell is a gamete, so it is haploid and has one set: 11 chromosomes. (Cambridge Supplement.)
workedSolution:
1. Leaf cells are diploid: 22 chromosomes = two sets of 11.
2. Gametes are haploid: one set.
3. The egg cell has 22 ÷ 2 = 11 chromosomes.
hints: Gametes have half the diploid number.

stem: Citrus growers in Zimbabwe usually plant grafted trees. A shoot of a sweet orange variety is joined onto a rough lemon rootstock.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which type of reproduction is grafting?

options.content: Artificial asexual propagation
options.rationale: No gametes are involved and humans carry it out.

options.content: Natural asexual reproduction
options.rationale: Grafting is done by people, so it is artificial.

options.content: Sexual reproduction
options.rationale: No gametes fuse in grafting.

options.content: Cross-pollination
options.rationale: Pollination involves transferring pollen, not joining stems.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Suggest two advantages to the grower of planting grafted trees rather than trees grown from orange seeds.

points.description: The fruit is identical to that of the good orange variety (same quality, taste, size)
Any second advantage: trees bear fruit sooner; the rootstock gives strong roots / resistance to soil diseases or drought; the trees are uniform

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain why the cut surfaces of the scion and rootstock must be held tightly together.

points.description: So that the tissues grow together and the xylem and phloem join, allowing water to reach the scion and sugars to reach the roots

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: State one disadvantage of growing a whole orchard of grafted trees of the same variety.

points.description: No variation, so a disease could affect all the trees; OR diseases (e.g. viruses) in the scion are passed on; OR grafting needs skill and time

explanation: Grafting is artificial asexual propagation. The fruit is identical to the scion's variety and trees fruit sooner on vigorous rootstocks, but an orchard of clones lacks variation and can share the same disease.
workedSolution:
**(a)** Artificial asexual propagation.

**(b)** Identical good-quality fruit; earlier fruiting or hardy rootstock.

**(c)** So that the transport tissues join.

**(d)** No variation: one disease could affect every tree.
hints: Are any gametes involved?

stem: Cassava is grown from stem cuttings. Cassava mosaic disease is caused by a virus; infected plants have twisted, mottled leaves and small roots.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Plants grown from cuttings of one parent plant are

options.content: genetically identical to the parent
options.rationale: Cuttings are clones of the parent.

options.content: genetically different from the parent
options.rationale: Cuttings involve no gametes, so no variation arises.

options.content: haploid
options.rationale: Cuttings have the same diploid nuclei as the parent.

options.content: produced by fertilisation
options.rationale: No gametes fuse when a cutting grows.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: State two advantages to a farmer of growing cassava from cuttings.

points.description: First advantage, e.g. the crop has the same good qualities as the parent (uniform)
Second advantage, e.g. faster than growing from seed; cheap (no need to buy seed); reliable (no pollination needed)

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain why farmers are advised to take cuttings only from healthy plants.

points.description: The virus in an infected plant is carried into its cuttings, so the new plants are infected from the start
The disease then spreads through the crop / reduces the yield of the whole field, because all the plants are equally susceptible

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Plant breeders use sexual reproduction when they want to produce a new cassava variety that resists the disease. Explain why.

points.description: Sexual reproduction produces variation / new combinations of alleles in the offspring
Some offspring may be resistant; breeders can select these (and combine resistance with high yield) and then multiply them by cuttings

explanation: Cuttings are clones: uniform, quick and cheap, but they carry the parent's viruses and all share the same susceptibility. Only sexual reproduction creates the variation from which resistant varieties can be selected.
workedSolution:
**(a)** Genetically identical to the parent.

**(b)** Uniform crop with the parent's qualities; quick and cheap.

**(c)** Viruses pass into the cuttings and spread through a crop of identical plants.

**(d)** Sexual reproduction gives variation; resistant offspring can be selected and then propagated.
hints: Where does the virus in a cutting come from?

stem: This question is about the number of chromosomes in human cells. (Cambridge Supplement)

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: How many chromosomes are in the nucleus of a human egg cell?

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: How many chromosomes are in the nucleus of a human zygote?

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Which of these human cells has a diploid nucleus?

options.content: A skin cell
options.rationale: Body cells are diploid, with 46 chromosomes.

options.content: A sperm cell
options.rationale: Sperm cells are gametes, which are haploid.

options.content: An egg cell
options.rationale: Egg cells are gametes, which are haploid.

options.content: A pollen grain
options.rationale: Pollen grains are found in flowering plants, not humans.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Explain why it is important that gametes are haploid.

points.description: When two gametes fuse at fertilisation, the zygote receives a set from each, restoring the diploid number (46)
So the chromosome number stays the same from one generation to the next (it does not double each generation)

explanation: Human gametes contain 23 chromosomes (haploid); the zygote and body cells contain 46 (diploid). Haploid gametes ensure that fertilisation restores the diploid number, keeping it constant across generations.
workedSolution:
**(a)** 23.

**(b)** 23 + 23 = 46.

**(c)** A skin cell.

**(d)** Fusion of two haploid gametes restores the diploid number, so it stays constant each generation.
hints: A human body cell has 46 chromosomes.

stem: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of sexual reproduction for wild plant populations and for crop production. [6]

points.description: Wild advantage: variation allows the population to adapt to environmental change / some individuals may resist a new disease (natural selection)
Wild advantage: seeds can be dispersed away from the parent (less competition, colonising new areas) and can survive unfavourable seasons
Wild disadvantage: needs two gametes to meet, often via pollinators or wind, so it may fail; it is slower and uses more energy (flowers, nectar, pollen)
Crop advantage: variation lets breeders select and combine useful features (e.g. drought tolerance, disease resistance) to make new varieties
Crop advantage: seeds are easy to store and transport
Crop disadvantage: offspring vary, so the crop is less uniform; seed saved from hybrid crops gives variable, lower yields, so new seed must be bought

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
In **wild populations**, sexual reproduction produces **variation**. If the environment changes or a new disease arrives, some individuals may survive and reproduce, so the population can adapt by natural selection. Seeds can be dispersed away from the parent, reducing competition and allowing new areas to be colonised, and they can survive the dry season. However, the gametes must be brought together, usually by insects or wind, so reproduction can fail, and producing flowers, nectar and pollen uses a lot of energy.

For **crops**, variation allows plant breeders to combine useful features such as drought tolerance and disease resistance into new varieties, and seed is easy to store and transport. On the other hand, the offspring are not identical, so the crop may be less uniform, and seed saved from a hybrid maize crop gives variable, lower yields, so farmers must buy new seed every season.

explanation: A balanced answer covers wild populations and crops, giving advantages (variation, adaptation, dispersal, plant breeding, easy storage) and disadvantages (needs pollination, slower, more energy, non-uniform crops, buying hybrid seed).
hints: Organise your answer in four parts: wild advantages, wild disadvantages, crop advantages, crop disadvantages.

stem: How does yeast usually reproduce asexually?

options.content: By budding
options.rationale: A small bud grows out of the parent cell and separates.

options.content: By runners
options.rationale: Runners are horizontal stems of plants such as strawberries.

options.content: By forming seeds
options.rationale: Seeds are produced by flowering plants after fertilisation.

options.content: By grafting
options.rationale: Grafting is a method of propagating plants.

explanation: Yeast is a single-celled fungus. It reproduces asexually by budding: a new cell grows as a bud on the parent and then separates.
hints: Think of a small growth that pinches off.

stem: Bean flowers are mostly self-pollinated: pollen from a flower lands on the stigma of the same flower, and seeds form. What type of reproduction is this?

options.content: Sexual, because a male gamete fuses with a female gamete
options.rationale: Any reproduction involving fusion of gametes is sexual, even within one plant.

options.content: Asexual, because only one plant is involved
options.rationale: Asexual reproduction involves no gametes; here gametes fuse.

options.content: Asexual, because no insects are needed
options.rationale: Whether insects are needed does not decide the type of reproduction.

options.content: Neither, because seeds are not offspring
options.rationale: Seeds contain embryos, the next generation.

explanation: Self-pollination is still sexual reproduction: pollen nuclei (male gametes) fuse with egg cells (female gametes) in the ovules. The offspring can still differ from each other because gametes are produced with new combinations of alleles.
hints: What defines sexual reproduction: the number of parents or the fusion of gametes?
